### Create emphysema/chronic bronchitis diagnosis phenotype
Apply the same method I used to create asthma diagnosis phenotype. So, I am going to use:

1. self-reported doctor diagnosed emphysema/chronic bronchitis in Data-Fields 6152;
2. self-reported doctor diagnosed emphysema in Data-Fields 22128;
3. self-reported doctor diagnosed chronic bronchitis in Data-Fields 22129;
4. primary care clinical records for asthma looking at Readv2 and ReadCTV3 codes in Category 3000 ('gp_clinical.txt');
5. hospitalisation data diagnosis for asthma looking at ICD-10 and/or ICD-9 codes (distinguish between all-level1-level2) in Category 2000 ('hesin_diag.txt');
6. primary cause of deaths for asthma looking at ICD-10 code in fields 40001;
7. secondary cause of deaths for asthma looking at ICD-10 code in fields 40002

ICD-9 codes for emphysema/chronic bronchitis : 491, 492
ICD-10 codes for emphysema/chronic bronchitis: J43, J40,J41,J42

I compared my clinical codes (Readv2, ReadCTV3, ICD9, ICD10) with Richard Packer's ones. Both for asthma and emphysema/
chronic bronchitis. For the latter, I used the clinical codes for COPD as an union of codes for emphysema/chronic bronchitis.
<br>
I implemented two analyses: a) I compared the clinical codes found by the two methods; b) Compare the participants with
diagnosed asthma and/or emphysema/chronic bronchitis using mine and Richard Packer's clinical codes.

### Readv2 and ReadCTV3 from data-coding 1834, 1835
Use resource from UK Biobank for both readv2 and readCTV3 codes mapped to ICD-10 codes:

 * data-coding 1834, readv2 into ICD-10;
 * data-coding 1835, readCTV3 into ICD-10

This clinical codes are retrieved mapping ICD-10 code only. In my analysis, I used both ICD-10 and ICD-9. Therefore,
it is not really comparable my analysis with these two fields. More, for asthma, I used the clinical code available
from the resource 'algorithm_outcome_codes.xlsx' table 'Asthma - P2' provided by UK Biobank. I then skipped this analysis
because not informative.

## Comparison with amalgamated asthma phenotype definition form Data-Fields 131495 and 131497
Data-field 131495 and 131497 use [data-coding 2171](https://biobank.ndph.ox.ac.uk/showcase/coding.cgi?id=2171).
These fields represent:

 * Data-Field 131495: 'Source of the first code mapped to 3-character ICD10 J45, and whether this code occurs in other source(s) with the same or a later event date. The code corresponds to "asthma".';

 * Data-Field 131497: 'Source of the first code mapped to 3-character ICD10 J46, and whether this code occurs in other source(s) with the same or a later event date. The code corresponds to "status asthmaticus".'

<br>
I cannot actually compare my number of participants for asthma diagnosis phenotype with theirs because UK Biobank made three analysis decisions
that I did not: looking at the date of the diagnosis, reporting the record in each category if it was the first diagnosis ever reported,
using Data-Field 20002 for self-reported asthma. Therefore, it is expected that my number of asthma diagnosed participant differs from theirs.

### Focus on hospitalisation inpatient data check
I have a high number of participants with an ICD-10/9 code for asthma in hospitalisation inpatient data.
I compare participants with hospitalisation data source as found by data-field 191495 (J45) and 191497 (J47) which
are amalgamated phenotype definition for asthma from 4 sources: Hospital in-patient records (ICD10 and ICD9);
Death records (ICD10); Primary care records (Read v2 and Read CTV3); Self-report ('Data-Field 20002 using mapping between
all reported diagnosed contribution to the 3-character ICD10 codes where appropriate';
[see Resource593](https://biobank.ndph.ox.ac.uk/showcase/refer.cgi?id=593))
<br>
Since this definition makes use of the diagnosis date while my asthma diagnosis definition does not, I cannot properly
compare my number of participants with hospitalisation record with theirs. In addition, they report a reduced number of participants
in the category 40 and 41, presumably because the hospitalisation would happen after a diagnosis of asthma firstly
reported in primary care data.
With my definition of asthma diagnosis, I retrieve 46308 participants with an asthma ICD-9 or 10 code in hospitalisation
record. The vast majority show an asthma code as a secondary cause for hospitalisation (45497), and 4021 participants show
asthma code as primary cause of hospitalisation. Overall, they represent the 10.5% of all participants with hospitalisation records
which is in line with the prevalence of asthma in the general UK population (~10% in the period 2008-2012) ( [NICE](https://cks.nice.org.uk/topics/asthma/background-information/prevalence/#:~:text=In%20the%20UK%2C%20over%208,have%20been%20diagnosed%20with%20asthma.))

## Clinical codes check
### Comparison clinical codes with Richard Packer's ones
#### Asthma
Total number of participants with Richard Packer's asthma clinical code is 150388, against the 80187 participants found
by my analysis. The datafield 20002 (self-reported asthma) adds 1260 participants not found by the other two datafield with
self-reported asthma (6125, 22127). Regarding clinical records, Richard Packer's clinical codes retrieved more
than the double of the participants I found (88411 against 29373). Hospital records show 67488 against 46308,
Richard Packer and my analysis respectively. Regarding primary and secondary death data, all the participants found
by my analysis are also found with Richard Packer's clinical code.

### Readv2 and ReadCTV3 from data-coding 1834, 1835
Data-coding 1834 and 1835 are based on ICD-10 only. I obtained

#### Observation: missing formatting in Readv2 and ReadCTV3 look-up table brought to a wrong code (00) in  my analysis
While checking for data-coding 1834 and 1835, I spotted a wrong code ('00') in the file 'ReadCTV3_Asthma_codes'. The problem
was due to the presence of the comma both as separator and as character in some column of the table 'read_v2_read_ctv3'
in the file 'all_lkps_maps_v3.xlsx'. Such code is a Readv2 for asthma, and it was retrieved by the searching, but then it
was uncorrectly reported as a ReadCTV3 due to mismatching of the column for the presence of the comma. Thus, I rewrote the
command leaving the comma just as separator and '00' was not retrieved as readCTV3 code anymore. The total number of individuals
with primary clinical code for asthma is now 29322 and the total number of participants with diagnosed asthma is 80138.
The number of distinct drug names becomes 49099 (49129 previously) resulting in 48039 distinct drug name (48069 previously) after a first
data cleaning (see [Medication_list.html](/home/n/nnp5/PhD/PhD_project/UKBiobank_datafields/scripts/Medication_list.Rmd)).
From 15484539 prescriptions and 38866 participants to 15480824 prescriptions and 38822 participants.
Genotyped individuals: with asthma diagnosis from 77651 to 77602; 15065507 prescriptions and 37846 participants to
15061792 prescriptions and 37802 participants.


# Conclusion

## Actions for Richard Packer's clinical codes
The number of participants retrieved by Richard Packer's codes is higher for both asthma and emphysema/chronic bronchitis.
I am not sure this clinical codes retrieve teh actual number of asthma participants in UK Biobank.
I will therefore use to define asthma the analysis and clinical codes as I implemented. I will exclude the participants found by
Richard Packer's clinical codes -both asthma and emphysema/chronic bronchitis- from the control in order to be sure that I will take participants free from asthma.
I could also run a sensitivity analysis using Richard Packer's asthma participants as case.
